blocks.content: Tap an option below to answer:
One codebase that adapts its layout to different screen sizes.
Exactly. One codebase, one set of files, and the layout adjusts based on screen width. No separate mobile site needed.
Exactly. One codebase, one set of files, and the layout adjusts based on screen width. No separate mobile site needed.
A separate website built only for mobile devices.
Teams used to do this, actually. They'd build a whole separate site at m.example.com just for mobile. Responsive design replaced that entirely.
Teams used to do this, actually. They'd build a whole separate site at m.example.com just for mobile. Responsive design replaced that entirely.
A design that only works on desktop.
If it only worked on desktop it wouldn't solve much, would it? The whole point is the same code works everywhere, it just looks different depending on the screen.
If it only worked on desktop it wouldn't solve much, would it? The whole point is the same code works everywhere, it just looks different depending on the screen.
A way to make images load faster.
Image performance is a real thing worth learning, but it's a separate topic. Responsive design is about how your layout adapts to different screen widths, not how files get downloaded.
